ev.q: The prevalence rate of diagnosed HIV infection in the Northeast (1,252.6) was 3.8 times that in the South
lower percentages of diagnoses in Hispanics or Latinos in Puerto Rico were among males (75.3% versus 84.1%)
In 2010, the overall rate of new diagnoses of HIV infection among Hispanics or Latinos in 46 states was 27.6 per 100,000 persons.
At the end of 2009, the overall prevalence rate of diagnosed HIV infection among Hispanics or Latinos was 432.3 per 100,000 persons.
The rate in the Northeast (55.0) was more than twice that of any other region
All of these reporting areas have had confidential, name-based HIV infection reporting since at least January 2007.

methods_quotes.q: The number of diagnoses of HIV infection was adjusted for reporting delay but not for incomplete reporting.
Multiple imputation was used to assign a transmission category to those cases missing risk information
was further adjusted to account for the delay in reporting of deaths among persons with HIV
Where possible, rates per 100,000 persons were calculated based on postcensal estimates of Hispanic populations from the U.S. Census Bureau
